details: Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson confirmed that September's inflation data led the FOMC to unanimously raise the federal-funds target by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00% on September 16, the first hike since 2023. Officials anticipate at least one more hike by end-2026, with inflation not expected to reach 2% until 2029, signaling a hawkish outlook due to persistent price pressures.
title: Fed Maintains Hawkish Stance, Projects Further Hikes Amid Persistent Inflation

details: The US 10-year Treasury yield surged about 18 basis points to approximately 5.1%, reaching its highest level since 2007. This rise followed robust business-activity data, which reignited inflation concerns and led to a broader risk-off sentiment across financial markets, including declines in crypto-linked equities and the cryptocurrency market.
title: US 10-Year Treasury Yields Surge to 2007 Highs, Sparking Risk-Off Sentiment

details: The total cryptocurrency market capitalization declined 5.15% to $2.87 trillion on September 24. Bitcoin fell 2.77% to $84,159, and Ethereum dropped 2.83% to $2,680. This market-wide correction was exacerbated by over $500 million in long liquidations and linked to broader macro uncertainty, including anticipation of the Trump–Xi summit and the impact of rising Treasury yields, despite continued institutional ETF inflows for BTC and ETH.
title: Bitcoin and Ethereum Lead Broad Crypto Selloff as Market Cap Falls 5.15%

details: Year-ahead inflation expectations in the United States, as measured by the University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, were confirmed at 4.6% in September 2026. This marks the highest reading since June and an increase from 4% in August, with long-run inflation expectations also rising to 3.4%. These elevated expectations underscore persistent price pressures, likely reinforcing a more restrictive monetary policy stance.
title: US Year-Ahead Inflation Expectations Jump to 4.6% in September, Highest Since June

details: On September 24, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) published updated FAQs clarifying how registrants and registered entities can engage with crypto assets and blockchain technology under the Commodity Exchange Act. The guidance permits futures commission merchants (FCMs) to utilize non-security crypto assets, including payment stablecoins, as margin and establishes capital charges for proprietary positions in Bitcoin and Ethereum.
title: CFTC Issues Updated FAQs on Crypto Assets and Blockchain Use by Registrants
